messages.subject: scaning for //
parts:
Hello all,

I'm trying to count the number of utterances in a file. Each utterance
is closed by a // symbol. Do you have suggestions as for how I can
clean a file of all numeric and alphabetic characters and count the //
symbols only?
After loading the file, the attempt was to perform the following
sequence of commands, but the result was integer (0):
(prii<-gsub("\\W", "", pri, perl=T)) and (x<-which(prii=="//"))


Thanks in advance, Heliana.

parts: > I'm trying to count the number of utterances in a file. Each utterance is closed by a // symbol. Do you have suggestions as for how I can clean a file of all numeric and alphabetic characters and count the // symbols only?

# No cleaning up with gsub is necessary:

corpus.file<-c("lvgnjero ivgn // uqbgveq qeu // ebneukbvebv", "blnewbn
klbn lkb nwklb n //",
"kbnl ebn lebn ln;lb nlwb // bn enbelbn le bn //", "vnelqnv elqnlqe
// juvbqeb //",
"e gejkleqljblbnklbnq //")
length(unlist(gregexpr("//", corpus.file, perl=T))) # find all instances of //

HTH,
STG

parts:
Heliana

This may not be an expert solution, but I can use gregexpr to help me
count sequences of "//":

prii<-c("//////")
positions<-gregexpr("//", prii, perl=T)
length(positions[[1]])
[1] 3

Using which == x counts the number of elements of a vector up to x

which(letters == "c")
[1] 3

John
